rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun answers his people's warning about piety in wealth God favored him with by becoming arrogant, admiring himself, and evading their demand.
rows.anchor: القائل قارون لما وعظه قومه وندبوه إلى اتقاء الله تعالى في المال الذي أعطاه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority say Qarun claimed knowledge that made him deserving of his wealth and favor.
rows.anchor: فقال الجمهور منهم إنه ادعى أن عنده علما استوجب به أن يكون صاحب ذلك المال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say he meant Torah knowledge and memorization, which they regard as deceitful display.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم علم التوراة وحفظها

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
rows.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani says Qarun meant experience and techniques for growing wealth, crediting his own discernment and effort.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداراني: أراد العلم بالتجارب ووجوه تثمير المال

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says he meant knowledge of alchemy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: أراد علم الكيمياء

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say Qarun claimed God had chosen him and granted the wealth through divine knowledge; “with me” means in his belief or opinion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وغيره: إنما أراد أوتيته على علم من الله وتخصيص من لدنه قصدني به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either way, the Qur'an exposes Qarun's delusion: God destroyed peoples and kings stronger than him and greater in amassed wealth or retinue.
rows.anchor: وعلى الاحتمالين معا فقد نبه القرآن على خطئه في اغتراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples exceeded Qarun in power and in wealth or surrounding followers.
rows.anchor: من هو أشد من قارون قوة وأكثر جمعا إما للمال وإما للحاشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Did he not know?” suggests Qarun boasted of his own knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أولم يعلم يرجح أن قارون تشبع بعلم نفسه

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb connects the clause to what precedes: each of the destroyed people is addressed and punished for what pertains to him.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن كعب: هو كلام متصل بمعنى ما قبله

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes this as a fresh statement about the Resurrection: criminals are not questioned about their sins.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هو إخبار مستأنف عن حال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they are not questioned because they enter the Fire without reckoning.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة ذلك لأنهم يدخلون النار بغير حساب

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatada and Mujahid say angels recognize criminals by darkened, disfigured faces and so do not question them, as in 55:41.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة أيضا ومجاهد: معناه أن الملائكة لا تسأل عن ذنوبهم لأنهم يعرفونهم بسيماهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an includes verses requiring questioning (37:24) and verses denying that people are asked (55:39).
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب الله تعالى آيات تقتضي أن الناس يوم القيامة يسألون

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: Some say the passages concern different stations and groups.
rows.anchor: فقال الناس في هذا إنها مواطن وطوائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers that questioning passages mean rebuke and confirmation, while denials mean requests for information; God already knows, and rebuke is not the informational questioning denied.
rows.anchor: ويشبه عندي أن تكون الآيات التي توجب السؤال إنما يراد بها أسئلة التوبيخ والتقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun displayed worldly power through clothing, mounts, and adornments when he came out before his people.
rows.anchor: وقد أظهر قدرته من الملابس والمراكب وزينة الدنيا

rows.speaker: جابر ومجاهد
rows.claim: Jabir and Mujahid say he went out wearing red garments.
rows.anchor: قال جابر ومجاهد: خرج في ثياب حمر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says Qarun and his company wore safflower-dyed garments.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: خرج هو وجملته في ثياب معصفرة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another report says purple garments; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says detailed accounts of Qarun's adornment lack sound basis and omits them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في ثياب الأرجوان، وقيل غير هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the verse shows how the foolish and inexperienced were dazzled by Qarun's display.
rows.anchor: وباقي الآية في اغترار الجهلة والأغمار من الناس بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who knew God, His due, and obedience rebuked the foolish people who wished for Qarun's position.
rows.anchor: أخبر الله تعالى عن الذين أوتوا العلم والمعرفة بالله تعالى وبحق طاعته

words: ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌۭ لِّمَنْ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They teach that aspirations should concern the afterlife: a believing, righteous worker awaiting God's reward is better than any possessor of worldly goods.
rows.anchor: أن النظر والتمني إنما ينبغي أن يكون في أمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This strength in goodness and religion is attained only by one patient in obedience and restraint from desires; it comprises all good.
rows.anchor: إلا الصابر على طاعة الله وعن شهوات نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to an antecedent unstated but clear from context, as in 38:32 and 55:26.
rows.anchor: والضمير من يلقاها عائد على ما لم يتقدم له ذكر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the pronoun refers to the saying that God's reward is better; only the patient receive and utter it.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري الضمير عائد على الكلمة قوله ثواب الله خير لمن آمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Qarun wronged Moses and accused him through a woman; Moses sought God's aid, and the earth swallowed Qarun and his followers gradually as they pleaded.
rows.anchor: أن موسى عليه السلام لما أمضه فعل قارون به وتعديه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the same report, God says He would have shown mercy and relieved them had they appealed to Him or repented.
rows.anchor: لو بي استغاثوا أو إلي تابوا لرحمتهم وكشفت ما بهم

rows.speaker: قتادة ومالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Qatada and Malik ibn Dinar transmit that Qarun sinks one stature each day until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومالك بن دينار: روي لنا أنه يخسف به كل يوم قامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “fiah” is a supporting group to which someone seeking help turns.
rows.anchor: الجماعة الناصرة التي يفيء إليها الإنسان الطالب للنصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode follows the sea crossing: transmitters said Qarun had preserved and recited the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقصة قارون هي بعد جوازهم اليم لأن الرواة ذكروا أنه كان ممن حفظ التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who had wished for Qarun's place regret it and recognize that power and strength belong to God.
rows.anchor: وندَمهم واستشعارهم أن الحول والقوة لله تعالى

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil take “way” as an attention marker, separate from “ka-anna” but joined in writing through frequent use.
rows.anchor: مذهب سيبويه والخليل أن «وي» حرف تنبيه

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: On their analysis, the expression calls attention, then introduces a report with amazement and reflection.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنهم نبهوا من خاطبوه ثم قالوا بين الاخبار وعلى جهة التعجب

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم وجماعة من النحويين
rows.claim: Abu Ḥātim and other grammarians derive “wayk” from “waylak,” with the lām dropped through frequent use.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم وجماعة من النحويين «ويك» هي ويلك

rows.speaker: عنترة
rows.claim: Antarah's verse is cited as evidence for the expression “wayk.”
rows.anchor: عنترة: [الكامل] ولقد شفى نفسي

rows.speaker: فرقة من النحويين
rows.claim: Another group treats “wayka'anna” as one indivisible expression meaning “alam tara anna.”
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة من النحويين ويكأن بجملتها دون تقدير انفصال كلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors separation, as Sibawayh does, since the element occurs with both “anna” and “inna”; Zayd ibn ʿAmr's verse supports this.
rows.anchor: ويقوى الانفصال فيها على ما قاله سيبويه لأنها تجيء مع «أن»

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads “lawla min Allah,” omitting “an”; a second narration has “lawla min” with nominative nūn and annexation to God.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «لولا من الله» بحذف «أن»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read “lakhasafa” with ḍamma on khāʾ and kasra on sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «لخسف» بضم الخاء وكسر السين

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads with fatḥa on both khāʾ and sīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم بفتح الخاء والسين

rows.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif read “la nakhsif,” a present tense depicting the earth swallowing them.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة بن مصرف «لا نخسف»

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is reported to pause after “way” and begin “ka-anna,” and also to connect the words like other readers.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الكسائي أنه كان يقف على «وي»

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported to pause at “wayk” and begin again at “anna Allah.”
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو أنه كان يقف «ويك» ويبتدىء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan allows “wayka'anna” or “yika'na,” with the hamza open or kasra, and likewise in “wayka'annahu.”
rows.anchor: قال الحسن إن شئت «ويكأن» أو «يكإن» بفتح الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Ibrahim” may coordinate with Nuh, with the pronoun in “We saved him” (29:15), or depend on an implied “remember Ibrahim.”
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون إبراهيم معطوفا على «نوح»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story is also an illustrative parallel for Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وهذه القصة أيضا تمثيل لقريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod and the people of his city worshiped idols; Abraham called them to God's oneness and worship.
rows.anchor: وكان نمرود وأهل مدينته عبدة أصنام فدعاهم إبراهيم إلى توحيد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read “takhluqūna ifkan.”
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس، «تخلقون إفكا»

rows.speaker: ابن الزبير وفضيل
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Fuḍayl read “ifkan” on the fiʿl pattern, a verbal noun like lying and laughter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير وفضيل «إفكا» على وزن فعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “you fashion falsehood” means making idols, named falsehood because people falsely claim they are gods.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس هو نحت الأصنام وخلقها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they fabricate lies about idols and other matters.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو اختلاق الكذب في أمر الأوثان

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن السلمي وعون العقيلي وقتادة وابن أبي ليلى
rows.claim: These readers use the doubled-lām form “wa-takhallaqūna ifkan”; in this reading “ifk” means a lie.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الرحمن السلمي وعون العقيلي وقتادة وابن أبي ليلى «وتخلقون إفكا»

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَمْلِكُونَ لَكُمْ رِزْقًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham argues from provision, familiar to all: idols cannot provide, so seek good from God; provision is singled out for its importance and stands for the whole category.
rows.anchor: ثم وقفهم على جهة الاحتجاج عليهم بأمر تفهمه عامتهم وخاصتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision is central to created life, and one part can signify its entire kind.
rows.anchor: فهو جزء يدل على جنسه كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “I thanked for you” and “I thanked you” are equivalent Arabic expressions.
rows.anchor: ويقال شكرت لك وشكرتك بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham concludes by informing them of the resurrection and return to God.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبرهم بالمعاد والحشر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that he discussed “a-innakum” elsewhere.
rows.anchor: تقدم القول في القرآن في أإنكم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says highway robbery was widespread among Lot's people.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: كان قطع الطريق بالسلب فاشيا فيهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says they intercepted travelers to pursue sexual misconduct and terrorize them.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: كانوا يقطعون الطرق على الناس لطلب الفاحشة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes this as cutting off procreation by abandoning women and having sex with men.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل أراد قطع سبيل النسل

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group says their infamous reputation made people avoid their roads and trade routes.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أراد أنهم لقبح الأحدوثة عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nādī” means a gathering place; it is generic because cities have many such places, meaning wherever people assemble.
rows.anchor: و «النادي» المجلس الذي يجتمع فيه الناس

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group says they pelted people with pebbles and mocked strangers; their gatherings lacked religion or propriety.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة كانوا يحذفون الناس بالحصباء

rows.speaker: أم هاني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umm Hāniʾ reports from the Prophet that they pelted and mistreated strangers; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives no grading.
rows.anchor: أم هاني عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد ومنصور
rows.claim: Mujahid and Manṣūr say they had sex with men in their assemblies while others watched.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومنصور: كانوا يأتون الرجال في مجالسهم

rows.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
rows.claim: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad says their indecency was sexual activity in their gatherings; al-Zahrawī transmits the view.
rows.anchor: وقال القاسم بن محمد: منكرهم أنهم كانوا يتفاعلون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they broke wind and slapped or clapped in their assemblies.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس كانوا يتضارطون ويتصافعون في مجالسهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also lists pigeon play, henna on fingertips, whistling, pebble-throwing, and general shamelessness.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد أيضا: كان أمرهم لعب الحمام وتطريف الأصابع بالحناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since some such acts occur among sinners in Muhammad's community too, mutual admonition against them is obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقد توجد هذه الأمور في بعض عصاة أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم فالتناهي واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's people answer his confrontation with denial and obstinacy, demanding punishment because they are convinced he is false.
rows.anchor: فلما وقفهم لوط على هذه القبائح رجعوا إلى التكذيب واللجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their challenge means they think the punishment will not come and Lot cannot bring it; such defiance reflects settled disbelief in him.
rows.anchor: وهم لم يقولوا هذا إلا وهم مصممون على اعتقاد كذبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot seeks God's aid, and God sends angels to punish the people with stones of baked clay.
rows.anchor: ثم استنصر لوط عليه السلام ربه عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels first came to Abraham bringing Isaac's glad tidings and news of aid for Lot; their meeting is described elsewhere.
rows.anchor: فجاؤوا إبراهيم أولا مبشرين بإسحاق ومبشرين بنصرة لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glad tidings comprise both Isaac and Lot's victory over his people.
rows.anchor: فلفظة «البشرى» في هذه الآية تتضمن أمر إسحاق ونصرة لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When told the town would be destroyed for wrongdoing, Abraham worried about Lot and argued about him in the following passage.
rows.anchor: أشفق إبراهيم على لوط فعارضهم بأمره حسبما يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the heavens and earth shows the insignificance of idols and every object worshiped apart from God.
rows.anchor: الذهن على صغر قدر الأوثان وكل معبود من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In truth” means with clear, rightful purpose, not play: creation displays sovereignty, confirms laws, places signs, and grants innumerable benefits.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: بالحق أي بالواجب النير لا للعبث واللعب

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands the Prophet to carry out His command and recite the revealed Qur'an.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر تعالى نبيه عليه السلام بالنفوذ لأمره وتلاوة القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means maintaining it and observing its limits.
rows.anchor: وإقامة الصلاة أي إدامتها والقيام بحدودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer restrains its practitioner from indecency and wrongdoing when performed with humility, remembrance, and awareness of standing before God's majesty; this reforms the self and its actions.
rows.anchor: وذلك عندي بأن المصلي إذا كان على الواجب من الخشوع والإخبات

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: An early Muslim is reported to tremble and turn pale at prayer, saying that standing before the King of kings warrants greater awe than worldly kings.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن بعض السلف أنه كان إذا قام إلى الصلاة ارتعد واصفر لونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer performed with this reverence necessarily restrains wrongdoing; prayer that only meets minimum validity leaves a sinner in his prior state.
rows.anchor: فهذه صلاة تنهى ولا بد عن الفحشاء والمنكر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن والأعمش
rows.claim: These authorities say prayer that does not stop indecency increases a person only in distance from God.
rows.anchor: الحديث المروي عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن والأعمش قولهم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also transmitted this as a mursal report from the Prophet, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya says its chain is unsound.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن الحسن أرسله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك غير صحيح السند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report does not mean the prayer itself is sinful; weak prayer fails to bring its owner nearer and leaves him persisting in sins that distance him.
rows.anchor: فغير جائز أن نقول إن نفس صلاة العاصي تبعده من الله

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: When told someone prayed often, Ibn Masʿūd said prayer benefits only one who obeys it.
rows.anchor: فقال: إنها لا تنفع إلا من أطاعها

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas reads that prayer commands right and prohibits indecency and wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الربيع بن أنس «إن الصلاة تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر»

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says “prayer” here refers to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر الصلاة هاهنا

rows.speaker: حماد بن أبي سليمان وابن جريج والكلبي
rows.claim: Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān, Ibn Jurayj, and al-Kalbī say prayer restrains only while one is performing it.
rows.anchor: وقال حماد بن أبي سليمان وابن جريج والكلبي: إن الصلاة تنهى ما دمت فيها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Anas reports that an Anṣārī youth prayed with the Prophet yet committed indecency and theft; the Prophet said prayer would stop him, and the youth soon repented.
rows.anchor: مما روى أنس بن مالك قال: كان فتى من الأنصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects “only while praying”: the Anas report shows prayer can bring later reform outside the prayer itself.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألم أقل لكم»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو الدرداء وسلمان وابن مسعود وأبو قرة
rows.claim: These authorities say God's remembering you is greater than your remembering Him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو الدرداء وسلمان وابن مسعود وأبو قرة: معناه

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another interpretation says persistent remembrance of God exceeds prayer in restraining indecency.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه ولذكر الله أكبر مع المداومة من الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd and Qatada say remembrance of God is greater than everything.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد وقتادة معناه ولذكر الله أكبر من كل شيء

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Asked which deed is best, Salman cites “the remembrance of God is greater.”
rows.anchor: وقيل لسلمان أي الأعمال أفضل؟ فقال: أما تقرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A report in the Muwaṭṭaʾ from Abū al-Dardāʾ begins, “Shall I tell you the best of your deeds?”
rows.anchor: ومنه حديث الموطأ عن أبي الدرداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the unrestricted sense: God's remembrance itself restrains wrongdoing, in and outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن المعنى ولذكر الله أكبر على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The part of remembrance in prayer has this effect, as does remembrance outside prayer; desistance requires a remembering, watchful person.
rows.anchor: فالجزء الذي منه في الصلاة يفعل ذلك وكذلك يفعل في غير الصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says that whoever remembers God in a gathering will be remembered by Him in a better gathering.
rows.anchor: ومن ذكرني في ملإ ذكرته في ملإ خير منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's physical movements do not restrain; useful remembrance requires knowledge, an attentive heart, and devotion, while tongue-only remembrance is lower.
rows.anchor: والحركات التي في الصلاة لا تأثير لها في نهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance of the servant is an infusion of guidance and knowledge's light, the fruit of the servant remembering Him, as in 2:152.
rows.anchor: وذكر الله تعالى العبد هو إفاضة الهدى ونور العلم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest is a warning and exhortation to watchfulness.
rows.anchor: وباقي الآية ضرب من التوعد والحث على المراقبة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read “ʿāqibatu” in the nominative as “kāna”'s subject; its predicate may be “al-sawā” or “an kadhdhabū.”
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو «عاقبة» بالرفع على أنها اسم كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “al-sawā” is the predicate, “an kadhdhabū” gives the cause; it cannot attach to “asāʾū” because that separates relative from antecedent by the predicate.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح تعلقه ب أساؤا لأن في ذلك فصلا بين الصلة

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī read “ʿāqibata” in the accusative as a fronted predicate.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «عاقبة» بالنصب على أنها خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Al-sawā” may be a verbal noun like “al-rujʿā,” or an adjective for an omitted “evil lot/outcome.”
rows.anchor: والسواى مصدر كالرجعى والفتيا والشورى

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abū Ḥātim describes the general reading with long wāw, open hamza, and feminine yāʾ; some readers use emphatic pronunciation and others imāla.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم هذه قراءة العامة بالمد على الواو وفتح الهمزة وياء التأنيث

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads “al-suwā,” doubling wāw without hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «السوى» بشد الواو دون همز

rows.speaker: الأعمش وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Masʿūd read the masculine “al-sūʾ.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وابن مسعود «السوء» بالتذكير

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān reportedly allows either “al-sūʾ” or “al-sawā.”
rows.anchor: وروي عن عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه أنه قال «السوء والسوأى» اقرأ بما شئت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “asāʾū” means disbelieved, “al-sawā” is Hell; denial of God's signs differs from mocking them, so both are named.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس أساؤا هنا بمعنى كفروا والسواى هي النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God proclaims universally that people will be resurrected from their graves.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى إخبارا مطلقا لجميع العالم بالحشر والبعث من القبور

rows.speaker: طلحة وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ṭalḥah and Ibn Masʿūd read “yubdiʾu,” with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة وابن مسعود «يبدىء» بضم الياء وكسر الدال

rows.speaker: جمهور القراء
rows.claim: The majority read “turjaʿūn” with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «ترجعون» بالتاء من فوق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The day” is accusative because it is governed by “yublisu.”
rows.anchor: وقوله ويوم منصوب ب يبلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Iblās” means being in evil while despairing of good in that very evil; the criminals despair in God's punishment.
rows.anchor: والإبلاس الكون في شر مع اليأس من الخير في ذلك الشر بعينه

rows.speaker: عامة القراء
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce “yublisu” with kasra on lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عامة القراء بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وعلي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and ʿAlī pronounce lām with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن وأمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه، بفتحها

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's expression “ablasa al-rabʿ” means a dwelling fell into ruin, as if it despaired of habitation.
rows.anchor: وأبلس الربع إذا بلي وكأنه يئس من العمارة ومنه قول العجاج

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌۭ
rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the sūra is Meccan except two verses, beginning at verse 27.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة أولهما: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

words: وَلَوْ أَنَّمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلَٰمٌۭ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says three verses are exceptions, the first beginning at verse 27.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ثلاث آيات أولهن ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the proud turncoat proves the disbelief of the man about whom the preceding verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: هذا دليل على كفر الذي نزلت فيه هذه الآية التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Waqr” is heaviness in the ear that makes sounds difficult to perceive.
rows.anchor: «الوقر» في الأذن الثقل الذي يعسر إدراك المسموعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is phrased as glad tidings because it is restricted and explicitly stated.
rows.anchor: وجاءت البشارة بالعذاب من حيث قيدت ونص عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After threatening disbelievers with the Fire, God mentions the believers' gardens to display the contrast.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر عز وجل حال هؤلاء الكفرة وتوعدهم بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Waʿda Allāh” is an accusative verbal noun, and “ḥaqqan” an emphatic verbal noun.
rows.anchor: ووعد الله منصوب على المصدر، وحقا مصدر مؤكد

rows.speaker: الحسن والناس
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan and most interpreters take the pronoun in “tarawnahā” to refer to the heavens: they have no pillars and are visibly so; the word is circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن والناس، وترونها على هذا القول

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn ʿAbbās take the pronoun to refer to the pillars: the heavens have unseen pillars, with “tarawnahā” an adjective in the genitive.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يعود الضمير على «العمد» فيكون ترونها صفة للعمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the first interpretation—that the heavens have no pillars and are visibly so—is sounder and the majority view.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الأول أصح والجمهور عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tarawnahā” may alternatively be nominative by interruption, with no pillars at all.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ترونها في موضع رفع على القطع ولا عمد ثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rawāsī” are mountains fixed firmly in the earth.
rows.anchor: و «الرواسي» هي الجبال التي رست أي ثبتت في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An tamīda” means “so that it not sway”; “mayd” is movement to either side and similar motion.
rows.anchor: وقوله: أن تميد بمعنى لئلا تميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Zawj” here means every type; lexically it means kind or class, not the opposite of an individual.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: من كل زوج أي من كل نوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Karīm” may praise fine construction and ordered beauty, encompassing every kind, or praise fine substance and appearance, referring only to choice things used as evidence.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: كريم يحتمل أن يريد مدحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We caused to grow” encompasses all kinds of animals, plants, and minerals.
rows.anchor: وقوله: «أنبتنا» يعم جميع أنواع الحيوان وأنواع النبات والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God challenges idolaters to show what their idols or other objects of worship created; they can show nothing, and their worship is manifest error.
rows.anchor: ثم وقف تعالى الكفار على جهة التوبيخ وإظهار الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charge of manifest error addresses Quraysh and also other nations who acted like them.
rows.anchor: بل هذا الذي قريش فيه ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mādhā” may have interrogative “mā” as subject and “dhā” as predicate meaning “that which,” with the relative pronoun understood.
rows.anchor: وقوله: ماذا يجوز أن تكون «ما» استفهاما في موضع رفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “mā” is the object of “arūnī” and “dhā” means “that which”; both parses imply “what they created.”
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون «ما» مفعولة ب «أروني»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God follows the disbelievers' state with the believers' state to clarify the difference and direct souls toward the better.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى حال الكفرة أعقب ذلك بذكر حال المؤمنين

rows.speaker: عامة القراء
rows.claim: The majority read “yuslim” with still sīn and ungeminated lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عامة القراء «يسلم» بسكون السين وتخفيف اللام

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسلم وأبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read with open sīn and doubled lām, meaning to devote, direct, and surrender oneself.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسلم وأبو عبد الرحمن «يسلم» بفتح السين وشد اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Face” is the bodily organ, borrowed for one's aim because a person pursuing something faces it.
rows.anchor: و «الوجه» هنا الجارحة استعير للمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doer of good combines speech and action, as the Prophet explained when Gabriel asked about ihsan.
rows.anchor: و «المحسن» الذي جمع القول والعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure handhold metaphor denotes a saving course free from failure; the believer clings to God's command as one clings to a hook.
rows.anchor: و «العروة الوثقى» استعارة للأمر المنجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Al-umūr” is the plural of “amr” meaning affairs, not the opposite of prohibition.
rows.anchor: والأمور جمع أمر وليس بالمضاد للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God consoles the Prophet: do not grieve at their disbelief, but continue the assigned proclamation; all return to God.
rows.anchor: فأمره أن لا يحزن لذلك بل يعمد لما كلفه من التبليغ

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group reads the quadriliteral form.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «يحزنك» من الرباعي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group reads the triliteral form.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «يحزنك» من الثلاثي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is in the breasts” means beliefs and opinions; two Arabic expressions about a wolf's belly and Abū Bakr illustrate the usage.
rows.anchor: و «ذات الصدور» ما فيها والقصد من ذلك إلى المعتقدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brief enjoyment is a person's worldly lifespan.
rows.anchor: والمتاع القليل هو العمر في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The severe punishment is intense and painful.
rows.anchor: و «العذاب الغليظ» معناه المغلظ المؤلم

words: وَلَئِن سَأَلْتَهُم مَّنْ خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters admit God created the world yet worship others; “praise God” means praise Him for making the proof clear.
rows.anchor: بأنهم يقرون بأن الله تعالى خالق المخلوقات ويدعون مع ذلك إلها غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rather, most of them” shifts from an omitted proposition such as “their claim is false.”
rows.anchor: بل أكثرهم إضراب عن مقدر تقديره ليس دعواهم بحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Most” is literal because Zayd ibn ʿAmr, Quss, and Waraqa ibn Nawfal were exceptions; it may also refer to those destined to convert.
rows.anchor: منهم من شذ فعلهم كزيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، وقس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns all in the heavens and earth; the idolaters' statements have no meaning or reality.
rows.anchor: بأن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض وما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs nothing for existence or perfection and lacks nothing in any respect.
rows.anchor: والغني الذي لا حاجة به في وجوده وكماله إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is praiseworthy in His essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: والحميد المحمود أي كذلك هو بذاته وصفاته
